hook.text: In 1950, Hamming was tired of restarting his computer every time a punch card had an error. So he fixed it.

buildup.text: Hamming codes place parity bits at power-of-2 positions. Each parity bit covers a specific set of data bits.

discovery.text: When an error occurs, the pattern of parity failures (the syndrome) directly points to the flipped bit.

twist.text: Hamming(7,4) encodes 4 data bits with 3 parity bits. It corrects any single-bit error automatically.

climax.text: ECC memory in every server uses Hamming codes or extensions to silently fix bit flips caused by cosmic rays.

punchline.text: Parity bits in the right places. Error located and fixed.

quiz.question: How does a Hamming code locate the error?
options: By analyzing the syndrome from parity check failures
